All seven scenarios hold, so I wrote `{"findings": []}` to `.run/validator/findings.json`. As instructed, I judged from the code and tests only and ran no build, test or git command.

- **`rust-plan`, across worktrees and with vcs off:** `crates/features/plan/src/next/number.rs` adds the numbers from worktrees, stacked approvals and `osq/` branches only when `vcs.enabled` is true. `crates/features/plan/tests/next_number_trees.rs` sets up a real `git worktree` and a branch with no worktree, and asserts the new folder is `021-a` with vcs on and `008-a` with vcs off. The base code only scanned the checkout, so the `021-a` test would fail on it. The `008-a` scenario isn't new behaviour; the base already gave that result.
- **`rust-storage`, "Trees of a project" and "Stacked trees":** `crates/kernel/storage/src/read/trees.rs` adds `change_trees`. `tests/change_trees.rs` checks all five table rows and confirms that `.stacked/002-b` is dropped because a worktree already names it.
- **`rust-storage`, "Changes across trees" and "Root alone":** the test for `list_tree_changes` checks the exact order of the four entries and which tree each comes from. It also checks that the root alone gives the same result as `list_changes`.
- **`rust-vcs`, "Stacked folder paths":** `crates/kernel/vcs/src/stacked.rs` handles a leading `~` alone and `~/`, and leaves `~other` as it is. `tests/stacked_root.rs` checks all four rows.

None of these test files could pass on the base, because the functions they call didn't exist before this change.

The two TypeScript tests in the patch (`tests/languages-lock-rebuild.test.ts` and `tests/vcs-sync-lockfile.test.ts`) come from the "sync main" merge of change 262. They don't relate to any scenario here, so I didn't judge them.
